title: Quant Surgery: Compact Cost-Latency-Fidelity Simulator
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, compact simulator (sheet-style) for quickly estimating per-request cost, median latency, and expected fidelity loss under different quantization regimes (INT8, FP8, and 4-bit) and micro-batching strategies. Not a canonical analysis — meant to be an engineering-first decision aid for SRE/product when we need a quick tradeoff recommendation in an incident or design review.

Quick usage notes (TL;DR):
- Drop in your workload profile (tokens per request, requests/sec burst shape, seq length distribution).
- Pick quant candidate (INT8 / FP8 / 4-bit) and kernel perf modifiers.
- Choose microbatch window and KV cache hit rate.
- Read off: amortized cost per 1k tokens, p50/p95 latency, estimated fidelity delta (ΔBLEU-like proxy).

Assumptions baked into model (editable):
1) Effective GPU token throughput base (fp32 baseline): 600 tokens/s per GPU for our reference long-context model (2B-7B style but used as generic baseline here).
2) Quant perf multipliers: INT8 = 1.6x throughput vs fp32, FP8 = 1.9x, 4-bit = 2.6x (these are starting heuristics from microbench runs; update after profiling).
3) Kernel latency floor (per-token) is modeled, plus per-request overhead (kv lookup, memmove, attention setup).
4) Fidelity penalty is approximated using a log-linear proxy: small Δ for INT8, moderate for FP8 on some ops, larger for 4-bit; we map these to a relative "fidelity score" in [0,1].
5) Cost is GPU-second priced; we use $3.50 / GPU-hour baseline for reserved dedicated pool (supports Dedicated pricing scenarios).

Core variables (what to fill):
- tokens_per_request: default 80
- avg_seq_len: default 512 (affects KV cache reuse)
- requests_per_sec (steady): default 10
- burst_factor: default 5 (peak / steady)
- kv_cache_hit_rate: default 0.35
- microbatch_window_ms: default 25 ms (continuous batching window)
- model_baseline_throughput_tokens_per_gpu_s: 600
- gpu_hour_cost_usd: 3.5
- quant_choice: INT8 | FP8 | 4bit
- perf_multiplier (auto from quant_choice)
- fidelity_penalty_score (computed)

Key equations used in cells (text form):
- effective_tokens_per_gpu_s = model_baseline_throughput_tokens_per_gpu_s * perf_multiplier * (1 - microbatch_overhead_factor)
- required_gpus = ceil( (tokens_per_request * requests_per_sec * seq_multiplier) / effective_tokens_per_gpu_s )
- amortized_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd = (required_gpus * gpu_hour_cost_usd / 3600) / (tokens_served_per_second / 1000)

Example scenario snapshots (these are prefilled examples you can change):

Scenario A — Latency-first (chat read heavy)
- tokens_per_request: 16
- requests_per_sec: 50 (burst 200)
- microbatch_window_ms: 10 (tight window, low batching)
- kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.6
- quant: INT8 (perf_multiplier 1.6)

Results (approx):
- effective_tokens_per_gpu_s ≈ 600 * 1.6 * (1 - 0.08) = 883 t/s
- required_gpus steady ≈ ceil((16 * 50) / 883) = 1 GPU (burst headroom required for p95)
- p50 latency ≈ 18 ms per request (compute + net); p95 ≈ 72 ms (burst queuing)
- amortized_cost_per_1k_tokens ≈ $0.014
- fidelity_score ≈ 0.98 (small expected quality delta)

Scenario B — Throughput-first (batch embed / long generation)
- tokens_per_request: 1024
- requests_per_sec: 1
- microbatch_window_ms: 200 (we allow batching)
- kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.1
- quant: 4-bit (perf_multiplier 2.6)

Results (approx):
- effective_tokens_per_gpu_s ≈ 600 * 2.6 * (1 - 0.03) = 1516 t/s
- required_gpus ≈ ceil((1024 * 1) / 1516) = 1 GPU
- p50 latency ≈ 720 ms (generation dominated)
- amortized_cost_per_1k_tokens ≈ $0.0023
- fidelity_score ≈ 0.84 (noticeable fidelity regression on some instruction-following tasks)

Fidelity heuristic (how we compute proxy):
- We map quant choice to a delta on a normalized fidelity axis. Then we apply a sequence-length sensitivity factor (longer context -> higher sensitivity for some ops).
- Example mapping: INT8 -> -0.02, FP8 -> -0.06, 4-bit -> -0.16. Sequence factor = 1 + (seq_len/1024)*0.3 (caps at 1.6).
- fidelity_score = max(0, 1 + base_delta * seq_factor * (1 - kv_cache_hit_rate))

Operational notes / gotchas:
- Microbatching improves GPU efficiency but harms p50 if window is > ~30ms for interactive workloads. For human-facing chat choose window <= 10ms when possible.
- KV cache hit rate heavily shifts effective tokens: a 20% delta in hit rate can change cost by 10–30% depending on workload shape.
- FP8 numbers are optimistic; hardware-specific kernels (A100 vs H100 vs newer) can change perf_multiplier by ±15%. Always profile before recommending to a customer.
- For Dedicated reserved pricing use lower gpu_hour_cost_usd; for hosted transient pricing bump it to market spot/ondemand rates.

Quick checklist before shipping a quant recommendation to a customer:
- Run the microbench profile on representative model (ENG-INFRA-5123).
- Validate fidelity on 100 exemplar prompts from customer eval set (not generic LM metrics).
- Re-run simulator with observed perf_multiplier and observed fidelity deltas.
- Decide rollout plan: canary 1% -> 10% -> 100% with automatic rollback if quality regressions above threshold.

Open questions / TODOs (for this doc):
- Replace crude fidelity proxy with small eval harness tied to per-customer prompt sets (roadmap item: product-optimize #45).
- Add a p95 queuing model (M/M/1 approximation currently used, which underestimates multi-server burst interactions).
- Add explicit per-request memory pressure model for KV sizing (affects ability to use 4-bit path for long-context).

Notes history / provenance:
- Concept sketched in an incident war room (Slack link above) where we needed a quick int8 vs 4-bit decision for a latency-sensitive customer.
- Uses baseline numbers from microbench session 2024-12-18 (see linked confluence page).

If you use this sheet and want it integrated into the Optimize product as a small modal calculator, ping Priya (product) and Riley (benchmarks) so we can validate numbers and produce a tiny API that reads customer workload profiles.
